correctness.rationale: The proof establishes a regenerative convolution for every finite time, then uses a coprime lattice renewal generating function to obtain exponentially convergent finite-atomic phase laws and their normalized sawtooth mean. Since B(zeta)=1/zeta+O(1/zeta^2), these are uncancelled simple poles arbitrarily close to the imaginary axis, contradicting analytic continuation under exponential decay of m(t)-1/2. Exact rational and complex-root computations passed 19,578 assertions; finite checks are supporting consistency only.

value.rationale: Incommensurate two-atom flight times are the minimal stochastic perturbation that breaks deterministic periodicity. Although nonarithmetic renewal theory ensures weak position mixing, it is not automatic that a chosen physical observable lacks exponential relaxation. Proving this for the mean itself, with explicit near-imaginary pole curvature and noncancellation, supplies a natural quantitative boundary for threshold-reset transport. The arithmetic comparison is not counted as new, and no downstream universal rate or experimental robustness is claimed.
